chapter: New York dance bands and Dorsey
title: Ray Noble's English and Bud as interpreter
summary: Freeman translates Noble's British phrasing for the band; a musician locked in a closet misses rehearsal and Noble says 'Didn't know, my ass.'

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: And Johnny Mince, of course, and so I say we were with that for 18 months, but when you turn this over, because the story I tell will take a few minutes. Ray Noble was not aware that English and American were
two different languages and actually I became interpreter because in my travels, I was sort of an Anglo-philé and I used to go. --
All right, Bud, you try this and we will get a shot on this.

I used to go see a lot of British plays when I was a kid and I got to understanding the language pretty well and liked English. So Ray would talk, you know, he was a Cambridge graduate and we had a radio show, the Coca-Cola Hour, which was quite a big thing in those days and Ray would get into the control room during rehearsals and give orders, talk out to the fellows, and he would say, 'Fellows, take the last eight bars and (unintelligible). They couldn't understand him. They'd come over and they'd say to me, Bud, what the hell did he say.?' So I would interpret. Ray, of course, and I became very close because he used to say to me, Bud, did you ever go to school in England?' and I said, 'No, I have seen a lot of films.' You know, when Hollywood got going in talkies, they sent to England for all the best theatre actors of course, and we were all brainwashed pretty much by the British speech, Dave Tough and I, you know. So anyway, a funny thing happened, Ray -- I think

it was Wilbur well, I didn't want to mention his name, I might say that one of the men in the band was having an affair with a married woman, and it was a habit every Tuesday morning to show up at the rehearsal at such and such a studio at CBS at 10:00. No one had to say the night before that we have a rehearsal tomorrow, you just automatically went there.
But he didn't show up for rehearsal because this woman's husband came home unexpectedly and she locked him in a closet -- her lover in a closet where he lay for about nine hours.

Luckily the husband left in the morning without finding the man, so he came out and he called the studio and now, the rehearsal is all over and he meets Ray somehow, he said, didn't know there was rehearsal so now Ray, threw his pen down and knocked the music over and said very angrily, 'Didn't know, my ass.'

Now, the Americans musicians had never heard that word used with a broad A and there was a sort of double take of thought and they fell on the floor rolling and laughing and Ray looked at me and he said, 'Buddy, what are the chaps laughing about?'
So it was really quite an hilarious experience being with Ray, because as I say, the musicians just could not understand him. And there was the proof of the two
